title: Domestic Relations Mediation / Settlement Conference
what_it_is: A nonbinding process in which a neutral mediator facilitates communication to promote settlement (MCR 3.216(A)(2)). All domestic relations cases are subject to mediation under this rule unless a statute or court rule says otherwise. If both parties request it and the mediator agrees, evaluative mediation (a written settlement recommendation) is available (MCR 3.216(A)(2), (C)(2)).
who_is_in_the_room: The mediator - a neutral third party, not a judge, not an advocate for either side.
You and the other party, and counsel if either has one.
sequence: The court refers a contested issue to mediation by written order, on stipulation, motion, or its own initiative (MCR 3.216(C)(1)).
A party who objects must file a written motion and notice of hearing within 14 days of receiving notice of the referral; the objection motion is heard within 14 days of filing (MCR 3.216(D)(1)-(2)).
Cases involving child abuse/neglect, domestic abuse (absent both attorneys present), inability to negotiate, or safety risk may be exempt (MCR 3.216(D)(3)).
The mediation session proceeds; if both parties requested evaluative mediation and the mediator agrees, a written settlement recommendation may issue at the end (MCR 3.216(A)(2)).
Any settlement reached is reduced to a written, signed agreement before it binds anyone.
prepare: A short list of your non-negotiable terms versus terms you would trade, in writing, before the session.
A copy of any existing order and your proposed changes with reasons.
If you believe mediation is unsafe or inappropriate given DV/PPO/CPS facts, raise the MCR 3.216(D)(3) exemption in writing before the session, not during it.

applicable_rules.summary: Domestic relations mediation is nonbinding; a written settlement recommendation (evaluative mediation) requires both parties' request and the mediator's agreement.
Cases may be exempt from mediation for child abuse/neglect, domestic abuse, inability to negotiate, safety risk, or other good cause.
An objection to referral to mediation must be a written motion plus notice of hearing, filed within 14 days of receiving notice of the referral order.

deadlines.label: Motion to remove the case from mediation
Hearing on a timely objection to mediation

traps.trap: Agreeing to something verbally in the room without it being written and signed.
traps.safe_move: Nothing binds until reduced to a written, signed agreement - do not treat a verbal concession as final.

traps.trap: Not raising a DV/safety exemption before the session.
traps.safe_move: MCR 3.216(D)(3) exemptions exist; raise them in writing, in advance, if applicable - do not wait until you are in the room with the other party.

traps.trap: Treating mediation as a place to relitigate the whole history.
traps.safe_move: The mediator facilitates settlement, not fact-finding; stay on the terms actually in dispute.

traps.trap: Assuming the mediator can be told things confidentially that will not shape the process.
traps.safe_move: Mediation records have their own confidentiality rule (MCR 2.412) but the mediator is still working toward settlement, not serving as your advisor - PROVISIONAL, confirm this mediator's specific confidentiality practice.

do_not: Never characterize the other parent with a clinical label as a pleaded claim (narcissist, alienator, PAS, coercive control) - GUARDRAILS.md S2.
Never use the child as a witness, messenger, interviewee, or source, and never record the child - GUARDRAILS.md S8, absolute.
Never assert that any recording you made is lawful - Michigan law is unsettled and the exposure is criminal.
Never sign or stipulate to anything on the spot without reading it fully first.

openers: Good morning/afternoon, Your Honor. My name is [Party], and I am representing myself.
I am here to address [narrow issue]. I have [N] exhibits and a short chronology.
closers: I don't have that information, but I can provide records if needed.
I'd like the record to reflect [narrow, factual point] and I reserve my right to address anything broader in the appropriate forum.

safety_gates: immediate danger -> 911, do not proceed on this guide alone
PPO/DV/CPS contact live -> stop, safety resources, do not proceed on this guide alone
UCCJEA/interstate fact -> stop, MC 416 affidavit guidance
recording question in any form -> unsettled law, criminal exposure, attorney question only
child asked/expected to speak to anyone about the case -> stop
exit_checklist: Write down the date, who appeared, and what was decided or taken under advisement before leaving the building.
Write on any document handed to you the date you received it - that date can start a clock.
Calendar every deadline this event started, counted from the earliest possible trigger date.
Note whether anything was requested that you did not have time to answer fully, and follow up in writing.
Get any agreement in writing and signed before leaving, or confirm the process for reducing it to a stipulated order.
